notes.1: S1/S2 split mid-quote by the cutter (…བསྒྲུབས་པའོ། | ཞེས་གསུངས་པ…); kept together as the opening point, ends as lead-in to the root verse.
notes.3: Six-line root verse: line 4 ends on connective …མཉམ་ཉིད་པས། and the sentence closes only at line 6 (…རང་བཞིན་ནོ།).
notes.9: Close of the verse plus the author's own question 'what do these words mean?' (…ཞེ་ན།); kept apart from the answer per rule 3.

notes.33: Question 'how essenceless?' (…ཅེ་ན།) is embedded mid-unit in S33, so it cannot be split from its answer.
notes.46: Author's question (…ཞེ་ན།) opening the 'no grasped object' topic; separate per rule 3.
notes.50: Author's question (…ཞེ་ན།) opening the 'no grasper' topic; separate per rule 3.
notes.51: S52 'why?' (…ཞེ་ན།) sits inside the sūtra quotation (addressed to Guhyapati), so it stays with its answer rather than splitting per rule 3.
notes.55: S59 ཞེས་སོ། closes a prose quotation, not a verse, so it stays within the paragraph; S60 re-quotes the root-verse lines as conclusion.

notes.75: Two 'why?' questions (S75, S78) are inside the continuing sūtra quotation; kept with their answers.
notes.80: S82 ཇི་སྐད་དུ། lead-in ends this paragraph per rule 5.
notes.87: One-sentence prose lead-in between two quoted stanzas; cannot join either verse block.
notes.92: ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། close attached forward to the next point (bodhicitta as root of all qualities) per rule 5.
